answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying identity to a refundable stake plus a verifiable work record, not a free account. Before transacting, an agent locks a bond and completes auditable tasks; cheating forfeits the bond, so each fake identity costs real capital. Bonds are graded like timber for load-bearing use and tested for ferrous-grade durability under stress, and only a proven record earns higher limits — the opal that survives inspection. Ten thousand Sybils then need ten thousand bonds, making mass fakery unprofitable while honest newcomers enter with one small bond.
